questions.explanation: The chlorination of methane to CCl4 proceeds via a free-radical substitution mechanism. Chlorine radicals abstract hydrogens stepwise, replacing them with chlorine atoms.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will give a positive test with Fehling's solution?
questions.explanation: Formaldehyde (and other aliphatic aldehydes) give a positive Fehling's test (red precipitate of Cu2O). Acetone, ethyl acetate, and acetic acid do not react.

questions.stem: What is the correct IUPAC name for (CH₃)₃C-OH?
questions.explanation: The IUPAC name is 2-methyl-2-propanol or 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Common name is tert-butyl alcohol.

questions.stem: Glycine is a unique amino acid because it

options.B: has a sulfur containing R group

questions.explanation: Glycine is unique because its α-carbon has two hydrogen atoms, making it achiral (no chiral center). All other standard amino acids have a chiral α-carbon.

questions.stem: Arrange the following compounds in order of decreasing acidity :
questions.explanation: Based on the answer, the order of decreasing acidity is (3) > (2) > (1). This would correspond to electron-withdrawing substituents increasing acidity: trichloroacetic acid > dichloroacetic acid > chloroacetic acid > acetic acid.

questions.stem: Which functional group has the highest priority in IUPAC nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids have the highest priority among common functional groups and take the suffix '-oic acid'. Lower priority groups become prefixes.

questions.stem: What is the daughter nucleus formed when <sup>214</sup><sub>82</sub>Pb undergoes beta (β) decay?
questions.explanation: Page 13 provides the example: '<sup>214</sup><sub>82</sub>Pb (parent) → <sup>214</sup><sub>83</sub>Bi + <sup>0</sup><sub>-1</sub>β (daughter)'. In beta decay, a neutron converts into a proton and an electron (beta particle), increasing the atomic number by 1 while the mass number remains unchanged.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about sucrose?

options.A: It hydrolyzes to fructose and glucose.

questions.explanation: Sucrose (table sugar) hydrolyzes to give equimolar amounts of glucose and fructose. It is a non-reducing disaccharide and does not undergo mutarotation.

questions.stem: Which group uses the suffix '-one'?
questions.explanation: Ketones contain a carbonyl group bonded to two carbons and use the suffix '-one'.

questions.stem: What is the primary method for extracting the pure forms of Group 1 elements?
questions.explanation: Page 4 states, 'They are highly reactive and their pure forms can only be extracted/prepared by electrolysis.'

questions.stem: What is the product of the reaction of sodium acetylide (HC≡CNa) with 1-bromopropane?
questions.explanation: HC≡CNa + CH3CH2CH2Br → HC≡CCH2CH2CH3 (1-pentyne) via SN2. The alkyl chain lengthens by three carbons.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common drying agent used to remove traces of water from an organic solution after extraction?
questions.explanation: Anhydrous magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) and sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) are common drying agents that absorb water from organic solutions. They are filtered off before evaporation.

questions.stem: What is the product of the reaction of ethylamine with HCl?
questions.explanation: Amines are bases and react with acids to form water-soluble ammonium salts. Ethylamine + HCl gives ethylammonium chloride.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds has been suggested as causing depletion of the ozone layer in the upper stratosphere?
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) like Freon-12 (CCl2F2) have been implicated in the depletion of the ozone layer. They release chlorine radicals in the stratosphere, which catalytically destroy ozone.

questions.stem: What is one specific application of Lithium mentioned in the document?

options.A: Used as a primary component in fire extinguishers.
options.C: Used in the production of potassium oxide for oxygen generators.
options.D: Used as an anti-oxidant in foodstuffs.

questions.explanation: Page 25 states: 'Lithium is used in small, long lifetime batteries.' Option A refers to hydrogen carbonates, option C refers to potassium, and option D refers to sodium nitrite.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for CH3-CH2-CH=CH-CH3?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 5 carbons (pentene), and the double bond is between C2 and C3, so 2-pentene. Numbering gives the double bond the lowest number.

questions.stem: Benzaldehyde reacts with a mixture of concentrated sulfuric acid and nitric acid to give
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde (CHO group) is a meta director (deactivating). Nitration gives m-nitrobenzaldehyde as the major product.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds show geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: CH3CH=CHCH3 (2-butene) shows geometrical isomerism because each carbon of the double bond has a methyl group and a hydrogen atom, allowing cis/trans forms. The other compounds either have no C=C or have identical groups at one end.

questions.stem: What is the definition of half-life in the context of radioactive isotopes?

options.A: The time it takes for an isotope to completely lose its radioactivity.
options.B: The time it takes for an isotope to lose half its radioactivity.
options.C: The time required for an isotope to double its radioactivity.
options.D: The average lifespan of a single radioactive atom.

questions.explanation: Page 9 states: 'The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the time it takes to lose half its radioactivity.'

questions.stem: Benzaldehyde reacts with methylmagnesium iodide (followed by hydrolysis) to form
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) reacts with methylmagnesium iodide (CH3MgI) followed by hydrolysis to give 1-phenylethanol (C6H5CH(OH)CH3).

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for acetic anhydride?
questions.explanation: Acetic anhydride is (CH₃CO)₂O. IUPAC name is ethanoic anhydride.

questions.stem: Why is BaSO₄ used in diagnosing stomach ulcers, as stated in the document?

options.A: It helps to heal the ulcers directly.
options.B: It acts as an antacid, reducing acidity.
options.C: It is insoluble in water and opaque to x-rays, allowing a shadow of the stomach to be seen.

questions.explanation: Page 15 explains, 'BaSO₄ is used in diagnosing stomach ulcers because it is insoluble in water and opaque to x-rays' and 'So it is used to provide shadow of the stomach on an x-ray picture.'

questions.stem: Hydrolysis of benzal chloride gives
questions.explanation: Benzal chloride (C6H5CHCl2) on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO). The two chlorine atoms on the same carbon are hydrolyzed to form the aldehyde.

questions.stem: What is the product of ozonolysis (O3 followed by H2O) of 2-butyne (CH3C≡CCH3)?
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of internal alkynes gives two carboxylic acids. 2-Butyne yields two molecules of acetic acid.

questions.stem: What type of bond is broken during addition reactions of alkenes?
questions.explanation: The weaker π bond is broken during addition reactions, while the sigma bond between carbons remains intact, allowing two new sigma bonds to form.

questions.stem: What is the bond length of a typical C=O bond?
questions.explanation: The carbonyl C=O bond length is approximately 1.23 Å, shorter than a C=C bond (1.34 Å) and much shorter than a C-C single bond (1.54 Å).

questions.stem: 2-Bromobutane reacts alcoholic KOH to mainly give
questions.explanation: 2-Bromobutane with alcoholic KOH undergoes dehydrohalogenation to give 2-butene as the major product (Zaitsev product, more substituted alkene).

questions.stem: 1,2-Ethanediol reacts with anhydrous zinc chloride to form
questions.explanation: 1,2-Ethanediol (ethylene glycol) when heated with anhydrous ZnCl2 undergoes dehydration to form acetaldehyde (CH3CHO). This is a pinacol-pinacolone type rearrangement.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of the Dumas method over the Kjeldahl method?
questions.explanation: The Dumas method is rapid (minutes) and can be fully automated, while Kjeldahl is slower (1-2 hours).

questions.stem: What is the C-C bond length in diamond?
questions.explanation: The C-C bond length in diamond is 1.54 Å, characteristic of a pure sp³-sp³ sigma bond.

questions.stem: What is a carbocation?

options.A: A carbon atom with 6 electrons and a positive charge
options.B: A carbon atom with 8 electrons and a negative charge
options.C: A carbon atom with an unpaired electron

questions.explanation: A carbocation (carbonium ion) is a carbon atom with only 6 valence electrons (three bonds) and bears a formal positive charge.

questions.stem: What is a crown ether?

options.A: A cyclic ether with a three-membered ring
options.B: A large cyclic ether that can complex metal ions

questions.explanation: Crown ethers are large cyclic polyethers that can selectively complex metal ions (e.g., 18-crown-6 complexes K+), making them useful as phase-transfer catalysts.

questions.stem: The sugar that yields only glucose on hydrolysis is
questions.explanation: Maltose (glucose-α-1,4-glucose) on hydrolysis gives only glucose. Lactose gives glucose + galactose, sucrose gives glucose + fructose, and fructose is a monosaccharide.

questions.stem: How many valence electrons does carbon (atomic number 6) have?
questions.explanation: Carbon's electronic configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p². The valence electrons are in the outermost principal energy level (n=2): 2s² 2p² → 4 valence electrons.

questions.stem: What is the name of the reaction that adds BH3 (borane) to an alkene, followed by H2O2/NaOH to give an alcohol?
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation is a two-step sequence: addition of BH3 (syn addition, anti-Markovnikov) followed by oxidation with H2O2/NaOH to yield an alcohol with OH on the less substituted carbon.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false about tautomers?

options.B: Tautomers are structural isomers which exist in dynamic equilibrium

questions.explanation: Tautomers do not have independent existence; they exist in a dynamic equilibrium with each other. The other statements are correct about tautomerism.

questions.stem: What is the product of the reaction between an amine and a carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: At room temperature, amines and carboxylic acids undergo an acid-base reaction to form a water-soluble ammonium carboxylate salt. Heating can convert this to an amide.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will not be easily oxidized?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation under normal conditions because they have no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH group. Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes/carboxylic acids, secondary to ketones, and aldehydes to carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: What is the term for a compound containing both a double bond and a hydroxyl group?
questions.explanation: Combining 'alkene' and 'alcohol' leads to the term 'alkenol'.

questions.stem: Which property makes carbon nanotubes exceptional for reinforcement?
questions.explanation: Carbon nanotubes have exceptional tensile strength (up to 100 times stronger than steel at one-sixth the weight), making them ideal for reinforcement in composite materials.

questions.stem: In succinic acid, HOOC(CH2)nCOOH, n is equal to
questions.explanation: Succinic acid is HOOC-CH2-CH2-COOH, so n = 2.

questions.stem: A wax is
questions.explanation: Waxes are esters of long-chain fatty acids and long-chain alcohols, and they are nonpolar solids. They are not triacylglycerols (which are fats/oils).

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is most basic?
questions.explanation: Benzylamine (C6H5CH2NH2) is most basic because the amino group is not directly attached to the ring (no resonance delocalization into the ring). Aniline is weaker due to resonance, acetanilide is weak (amide), and p-nitroaniline is very weak (electron-withdrawing nitro group).

questions.stem: Why do metals in the lower half of Group 1 tend to form more complicated oxides (peroxides and superoxides)?

options.A: Because their metal ions are small and have a high charge density.
options.B: Because the formation of these oxides releases more energy, making the system more energetically stable.
options.C: Because they have a higher electronegativity.
options.D: Because they are less reactive than the top elements.

questions.explanation: Page 9 explains, 'The formation of more complicated oxides (i.e. peroxides and superoxides) from the metals releases more energy and makes the system more energetically stable.' It also mentions these metals have big ions and low charge density.

questions.stem: What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound with the formula C₆H₅-CH₂-CH₂-OH?
questions.explanation: 2-Phenylethanol (IUPAC) and phenethyl alcohol (common) are correct. It has an OH on a two-carbon chain attached to a phenyl ring.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for the alkane with the formula C3H8?
questions.explanation: C3H8 is propane, the third member of the alkane series.

questions.stem: The reagent needed to convert 2-butyne to cis-2-butene is :
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation of 2-butyne with H2 and Lindlar's catalyst (Pd/BaSO4 poisoned with quinoline) gives cis-2-butene via syn addition of H2. This is a selective partial hydrogenation.

questions.stem: A compound, C15H24, is reacted with excess hydrogen using a metal catalyst. One equivalent of the compound consumed three equivalents of hydrogen. How many rings did the original compound have?
questions.explanation: The formula C15H24 has a degree of unsaturation (DBE) = (2C+2-H)/2 = (30+2-24)/2 = 8/2 = 4. Three equivalents of H2 consumed means 3 degrees of unsaturation are from double/triple bonds (each H2 adds to a π bond). The remaining 1 degree of unsaturation must be from a ring. So the compound has 1 ring.

questions.stem: Markovnikov's addition of HBr is not applicable to
questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule applies to unsymmetrical alkenes where the two carbons of the double bond have different numbers of hydrogens. 2-Butene (CH3CH=CHCH3) is symmetrical, so both carbons have the same number of hydrogens. Markovnikov's rule is not needed (or applicable) because addition to either carbon gives the same product.

questions.stem: What is the product of the reaction between benzoyl chloride and water?
questions.explanation: C6H5COCl + H2O → C6H5COOH + HCl. Acid chlorides hydrolyze to carboxylic acids.

questions.stem: Which hybrid orbitals are used by nitrogen in ammonia (NH₃)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in ammonia is sp³ hybridized with three bonding pairs and one lone pair, giving trigonal pyramidal geometry.

questions.stem: In Liebig's combustion method, what absorbs the carbon dioxide produced?
questions.explanation: CO₂ is absorbed by KOH solution (or soda lime) in a U-tube; the increase in mass gives the amount of CO₂ produced.

questions.stem: Regarding the allotropes of Carbon, which of the following statements is false?

options.A: Diamond is sp³ hybridized and a non-conductor of electricity.
options.B: Graphite is sp² hybridized and has a layered structure with delocalized electrons.
options.C: Graphite is brittle and soft, and conducts electricity along its layers.
options.D: Diamond has a lower melting point than graphite due to weaker covalent bonds.

questions.explanation: Page 11 states that diamond 'Has high mpt because both intermolecular and intramolecular bonds are covalent bonds..' and 'It is extremely hard, non-conductor and chemically inert'. Diamond forms a giant molecular structure with strong covalent bonds throughout, resulting in a very high melting point. Graphite also has a high melting point, but the statement implies diamond's would be lower, which is incorrect.

questions.stem: Which of the statements is correct about diastereomers?

options.A: They are stereoisomers that are not enantiomers.
options.B: They are a pair of identical isomers.
options.C: They are a pair of isomers that are mirror images.
options.D: All their asymmetric centers are the same.

questions.explanation: Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other. They are not enantiomers. They have different physical and chemical properties.

questions.stem: Combustion of an alkene with sufficient oxygen will produce
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of any hydrocarbon (including alkenes) with sufficient oxygen produces carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O).

questions.stem: A compound reacts with steam in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 to give isopropyl alcohol. The compound could be
questions.explanation: Isopropyl alcohol (propan-2-ol, (CH3)2CHOH) is formed by the hydration of propene (CH3CH=CH2) in the presence of acid. The addition of water follows Markovnikov's rule, giving the more substituted alcohol.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures can polypeptides have?
questions.explanation: Polypeptides can have all four levels of protein structure: primary (amino acid sequence), secondary (α-helix/β-sheet), tertiary (3D folding), and quaternary (subunit arrangement).

questions.stem: How do the monoxides of Group 14 elements (MO) generally compare in basicity to their dioxides (MO₂)?

options.A: Monoxides are generally less basic than dioxides.
options.B: Monoxides are generally more basic than dioxides.
options.C: Monoxides and dioxides have similar basicity.
options.D: Monoxides are always acidic, while dioxides are always basic.

questions.explanation: Page 18 explicitly states: 'The monoxides are more basic than the dioxides.' This is a general trend where lower oxidation states tend to be more basic.

questions.stem: Which of the following reagents will react with propene?
questions.explanation: Hot alkaline KMnO4 (strong oxidizing agent) will oxidize propene (an alkene) to cleavage products (carboxylic acids and CO2). Sodium metal, cold dilute HNO3, and LiAlH4 do not typically react with alkenes.

questions.stem: Which statement about the carbon-carbon double bond length is correct?

options.C: C=C and C-C are the same length

questions.explanation: The C=C double bond is approximately 1.34 Å, shorter than a C-C single bond (1.54 Å) due to the additional π bond pulling the carbons closer.

questions.stem: The isomers of a substance must have
questions.explanation: All isomers have the same molecular formula and therefore the same molecular weight. They have different structural formulas and may have different chemical properties and functional groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following amines has the highest boiling point for similar molecular weight?
questions.explanation: Primary and secondary amines can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds (N-H···N), increasing boiling points. Tertiary amines lack N-H bonds and have lower boiling points.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a valid method to prepare an alkyne from a vicinal dihalide?

options.A: Double dehydrohalogenation with strong base (e.g., NaNH2)

questions.explanation: A vicinal dihalide undergoes two successive E2 eliminations with a strong base like NaNH2 to form an alkyne.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best leaving group?
questions.explanation: The best leaving group is the one that can best stabilize the negative charge. Iodide (I-) is the largest, most polarizable, and least basic, making it the best leaving group among halides.

questions.stem: The hybridization of nitrogen in an amine is
questions.explanation: The nitrogen in amines is sp3 hybridized with a trigonal pyramidal geometry (similar to ammonia). It has three sigma bonds and one lone pair.

questions.stem: What is the industrial preparation of ethanal (acetaldehyde) from ethyne?
questions.explanation: Ethyne (HC≡CH) undergoes hydration with HgSO₄/H₂SO₄ to give ethanal (vinyl alcohol tautomerizes to acetaldehyde).

questions.stem: What is the suffix for a ketone in IUPAC nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Ketones have the suffix '-one' (e.g., propanone, butanone).

questions.stem: What is the product when a secondary aliphatic amine reacts with nitrous acid (HNO2)?
questions.explanation: Secondary amines react with HNO2 to form N-nitrosoamines (R2N-N=O), which are usually yellow oils and are potent carcinogens.

questions.stem: What does a 'curved' arrow represent?

options.A: that two structures are resonance structures
options.C: a link between reactants and products

questions.explanation: A curved arrow in organic chemistry specifically represents the movement of a pair of electrons (two electrons) from one atom to another, or from a bond to an atom, etc.

questions.stem: What is the temperature range for catalytic hydrogenation using nickel?
questions.explanation: Nickel requires higher temperature (250-300°C) for hydrogenation, unlike Pt/Pd which work at room temperature.

questions.stem: Which of the following reactions allows the synthesis of an internal alkyne from a terminal alkyne?

options.C: Alkylation of acetylide ion with a primary alkyl halide

questions.explanation: Acetylide ions (R-C≡C⁻) undergo SN2 reaction with primary alkyl halides to form internal alkynes (R-C≡C-R′).

questions.stem: Which of the following will give acetic acid on acid-hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: Ethyl acetate (CH3COOC2H5) undergoes acid-hydrolysis to give acetic acid (CH3COOH) and ethanol. Acetone is a ketone, methyl propionate gives propionic acid, and lactic acid is already an acid.

questions.stem: What are the products when lithium hydride (LiH) reacts with water (H₂O)?
questions.explanation: Page 11 provides the reaction: 'LiH(s) + H₂O(l) → LiOH(aq) + H₂(g)'.

questions.stem: What is the general trend for the thermal stability of Group 1 carbonates as you move down the group?

options.A: Thermal stability decreases down the group.
options.B: Thermal stability increases down the group.
options.C: Thermal stability remains constant down the group.
options.D: Thermal stability is unpredictable and varies irregularly.

questions.explanation: Page 18 states: 'Thermal stability increases down the group as size of the metal increases.'

questions.stem: What is the product when 2‑butyne is reduced with Na/NH₃ (liquid)?
questions.explanation: Dissolving‑metal reduction (Na/NH₃) gives anti addition, producing the trans‑alkene.

questions.stem: Starch

options.D: is a mixture of amylose + amylopectin.

questions.explanation: Starch is a polysaccharide that is a mixture of two components: amylose (linear) and amylopectin (branched).

questions.stem: What is the correct order of functional group priority (highest to lowest)?

options.A: Carboxylic acid > Ester > Amide > Nitrile > Aldehyde

questions.explanation: Priority order: Carboxylic acid > Ester > Amide > Nitrile > Aldehyde > Ketone > Alcohol > Amine > Alkene > Alkyne.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for (CH₃CH₂)₂NH?
questions.explanation: The IUPAC name for (CH₃CH₂)₂NH is N-ethylethanamine. The longest chain is ethane (2 carbons) with an ethyl substituent on nitrogen.

questions.stem: What is the product of the oxidation of a secondary alcohol?
questions.explanation: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol (R-CHOH-R') gives a ketone (R-CO-R') regardless of the oxidizing agent used.

questions.stem: Which statement about the structure of benzene is not true?

options.A: The two Kekule structures of benzene are in equilibrium.
options.B: The carbon-carbon bond lengths in benzene are greater than the carbon-carbon double bonds in aliphatic compounds.
options.C: The molecular geometry of benzene is best described as planar.
options.D: The stability of benzene ring is much greater than the stability of 1,3,5-cycloheptatriene.

questions.explanation: Neither of the two Kekule structures for benzene has been isolated. No equilibrium exists between these two structures because they are resonance structures, differing only in the positions of electrons. The other statements are true.

questions.stem: The reaction of a Grignard reagent with a ketone followed by acidic workup yields:
questions.explanation: Ketone (R2C=O) reacts with RMgX to give a tertiary alcohol (R2C(OH)R) after workup.

questions.stem: In Liebig's combustion method, what absorbs the water produced?
questions.explanation: Anhydrous CaCl₂ absorbs water vapor produced from combustion, allowing its mass increase to be measured for hydrogen calculation.

questions.stem: Plane-polarized light is affected by
questions.explanation: Plane-polarized light is rotated by chiral molecules (optically active compounds). Identical molecules, polymers in general, and all biomolecules are not all chiral or optically active.

questions.stem: Cyclobutane reacts with hydrogen in the presence of nickel catalyst at 200°C to give
questions.explanation: Cyclobutane undergoes hydrogenolysis with H2/Ni at 200°C to give butane (n-butane). The ring is opened and hydrogenated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical physical property of amines?

options.B: Low molecular weight amines are gases
options.C: They are nonpolar and insoluble in water

questions.explanation: Low molecular weight amines are polar and soluble in water due to hydrogen bonding. Higher molecular weight amines are less soluble, but smaller amines are quite water-soluble.

questions.stem: What happens when a 3° alcohol is treated with Lucas reagent?

options.B: Rapid formation of an insoluble alkyl chloride (cloudiness within 1 min)

questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react immediately via SN1 to form the corresponding alkyl chloride, which is insoluble and appears as cloudiness.

questions.stem: In the Gabriel synthesis, phthalimide is used to prepare:
questions.explanation: Gabriel synthesis uses phthalimide to produce pure primary amines from alkyl halides without contamination by secondary or tertiary amines.

questions.stem: What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound with two OH groups on carbons 1 and 2 of ethane?
questions.explanation: When an alcohol contains two OH groups, the suffix -diol is used with the alkane name. 1,2-ethanediol is the IUPAC name.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of cupric oxide (CuO) in Liebig's combustion method?

options.C: To act as an oxidizing agent to ensure complete combustion

questions.explanation: Cupric oxide provides oxygen to ensure complete combustion of the organic sample, especially when the sample contains elements that are difficult to oxidize fully.

questions.stem: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with phenol to form :
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol in alkaline solution to form p-hydroxyazobenzene (azo dye). This is a diazo coupling reaction.

questions.stem: A sample of pure amine molecules is found to possess no intermolecular H-bonding. This sample is most likely :
questions.explanation: Tertiary amines (3°) do not have any N-H bonds, so they cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other. Primary and secondary amines have N-H bonds and can hydrogen bond.

questions.stem: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in CH3NH2?
questions.explanation: The carbon in methylamine (CH3NH2) is sp3 hybridized because it forms four sigma bonds (three C-H and one C-N).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect about benzene?

options.A: All of the carbon atoms are sp hybridized.
options.C: The carbon-carbon bond lengths are all the same.
options.D: All twelve atoms lie in the same plane.

questions.explanation: All carbon atoms in benzene are sp2 hybridized (not sp). The other statements are correct: benzene has delocalized electrons, all C-C bonds are equal in length, and all atoms are planar.

questions.stem: What does the unit Sievert (Sv) represent in the context of radioactivity, according to the document?

options.C: 1 J of energy received by 1 kg of tissue

questions.explanation: Page 5, in the 'Units of radioactivity' table, defines Sievert (Sv) as 'Gray × quality factor of radiation'.

questions.stem: What functional group is represented by $-NH_2$?
questions.explanation: The amino group designates the amine functional group.

questions.stem: What is the correct IUPAC name for CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: The chain has 4 carbons with a methyl on C3, OH on C1. Both 3-methyl-1-butanol and 3-methylbutan-1-ol are correct.

questions.stem: Choose the correct hybridization for the atom indicated in the molecule below.
questions.explanation: Based on the answer, the indicated carbon atom is bonded to four other atoms via single bonds, making it sp3 hybridized.

questions.stem: What is the product when an unsymmetrical alkene undergoes anti‑Markovnikov addition of HBr in the presence of peroxides?

options.A: The same as the Markovnikov product
options.B: The bromine adds to the less substituted carbon
options.C: The product is always a tertiary alkyl bromide

questions.explanation: Peroxide effect (free‑radical addition) gives anti‑Markovnikov orientation: Br adds to the less substituted carbon.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most stable carbanion?
questions.explanation: Methyl carbanion is the most stable because alkyl groups are electron-donating and destabilize the negative charge; less substitution gives greater stability for carbanions.

questions.stem: According to the document, which element is considered the actual first member of Group 1, despite hydrogen often being placed there?
questions.explanation: Page 3 states, 'Although hydrogen (H) is the first element in the periodic table and is usually placed in group 1, the actual first member of group 1 is lithium.'

questions.stem: Which of the following is a terminal functional group?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes (-CHO) and carboxylic acids (-COOH) are always at the end of a carbon chain (terminal).

questions.stem: What does Schiff's test detect?
questions.explanation: Schiff's reagent (decolorized magenta dye) turns pink/magenta in the presence of aldehydes. Ketones generally do not react.

questions.stem: The separation of a mixture of two immiscible liquids can also be achieved by simple decantation. When is decantation preferred over using a separatory funnel?

options.A: When the two layers have similar densities
options.B: When a large volume of liquid is present and a separatory funnel is not available
options.C: When one layer is very small

questions.explanation: Decantation is simple pouring off the top layer. It is less precise than using a separatory funnel but useful when a separatory funnel is unavailable or when large volumes are handled.

questions.stem: How many bonds must every carbon atom have in a structural drawing?
questions.explanation: Carbon is tetravalent, meaning it must form four bonds to be stable.

questions.stem: In catalytic hydrogenation of a ketone with H2/Raney nickel, what is formed?
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation adds H2 across the C=O bond of a ketone, producing a secondary alcohol (R-CHOH-R').

questions.stem: What are the three rules for writing electron configurations (order of filling)?

options.B: Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, Hund's rule
options.C: Coulomb's law, Newton's law, Boyle's law
options.D: Markovnikov's rule, Zaitsev's rule, Hammond's postulate

questions.explanation: The three fundamental rules for electron configuration are: Aufbau (fill lowest energy first), Pauli (no two electrons same quantum numbers), and Hund (maximize spin before pairing).

questions.stem: What is the correct name for the compound HOCH₂CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: 1,2-Ethanediol is the IUPAC name; ethylene glycol is the common name. It is a diol (two OH groups).

questions.stem: What is the nature of an alpha (α) ray, as described in the document?
questions.explanation: The 'Properties of radiation' table on page 4, under the 'Nature' row for Alpha (α) rays, describes them as 'Helium nuclei <sup>4</sup><sub>2</sub>He'.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a metal catalyst for the hydrogenation of an alkene?
questions.explanation: Sodium (Na) is not a hydrogenation catalyst. Palladium (Pd), platinum (Pt), and nickel (Ni) are commonly used metal catalysts for catalytic hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes.

questions.stem: What is a halohydrin?

options.A: An alcohol with a halogen on the same carbon
options.B: A compound containing both a halogen and an OH group on adjacent carbons

questions.explanation: A halohydrin is formed by addition of X2 and H2O to an alkene, adding X and OH across the double bond, giving a halogen on one carbon and OH on the adjacent carbon.

questions.stem: What is the product of the reaction of sodium phenoxide (C6H5O-Na+) with methyl iodide?
questions.explanation: This is a Williamson ether synthesis: C6H5O- + CH3I → C6H5OCH3 + NaI. The product is methyl phenyl ether (anisole).

questions.stem: Bromobenzene can be prepared by treating aniline with
questions.explanation: Bromobenzene can be prepared from aniline via diazotization followed by Sandmeyer reaction with CuBr. Aniline → diazonium salt → bromobenzene.

questions.stem: What is the leaving group in the nucleophilic acyl substitution of an ester?
questions.explanation: When an ester undergoes nucleophilic acyl substitution, the alkoxide (RO-) is the leaving group.

questions.stem: What type of an alkyl group is an isobutyl group?
questions.explanation: The isobutyl group (2-methylpropyl, -CH2-CH(CH3)2) is a primary alkyl group because the point of attachment (the carbon bonded to the main chain) is a primary carbon (bonded to only one other carbon).

questions.stem: The combustion of one mole of propane, C3H8, produces how many moles of H2O?
questions.explanation: The balanced combustion equation for propane is C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O. Therefore, one mole of propane produces 4 moles of water.

questions.stem: Aliphatic primary amines react with cold nitrous acid to form
questions.explanation: Aliphatic primary amines react with cold nitrous acid (HNO2) to form alcohols (and nitrogen gas). Aromatic primary amines form diazonium salts under these conditions.

questions.stem: How many isomers are possible for pentane?
questions.explanation: Pentane (C5H12) has three structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

questions.stem: The appearance of a silver mirror in Tollens' test indicates the presence of :
questions.explanation: A silver mirror in Tollens' test indicates the presence of an aldehyde. Aldehydes are oxidized by Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal AgNO3) to carboxylic acids, depositing metallic silver.

questions.stem: Acetophenone reacts with Br2 in the presence of FeCl3 to form :
questions.explanation: Acetophenone (COCH3 group) is a meta director. Bromination gives m-bromoacetophenone as the major product.

questions.stem: The delocalized π system in benzene is formed by a cyclic overlap of 6 orbitals.
questions.explanation: The delocalized π system in benzene is formed by the cyclic overlap of six unhybridized p orbitals (one on each carbon), which overlap sideways to form a continuous ring of electron density above and below the plane.

questions.stem: Which statement about the carbon-carbon triple bond is FALSE?

options.A: It is shorter than a C=C bond
options.B: It consists of one σ and two π bonds
options.C: Free rotation is possible around the triple bond

questions.explanation: Free rotation is NOT possible around a triple bond (or double bond) because the π bonds would have to break. However, the linear geometry means rotation doesn't change the structure, but it's still restricted.

questions.stem: In recrystallization, a suitable solvent should have which property?

options.A: Compound is soluble in cold but insoluble in hot
options.B: Compound is soluble in hot and insoluble in cold
options.C: Compound is equally soluble at all temperatures

questions.explanation: For recrystallization, the compound should be very soluble in the hot solvent but sparingly soluble in the cold solvent. This allows the compound to crystallize out upon cooling.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for CH3CH2C≡CH?
questions.explanation: The longest chain containing the triple bond has 4 carbons (but-), with the triple bond starting at carbon 1, hence 1-butyne.
